title: X Monitoring
searchIntent: grok bot to monitor x mentions
intro: Grok Bot has first-party access to X, which makes this one of the few jobs where the platform advantage is real rather than incidental — these bots can search posts, read timelines and pull trends without a scraping arrangement that breaks. The listings cover mention tracking, reply triage, buying-signal detection and keeping an eye on specific accounts. The category divides on whether the bot writes. Watching is low-risk and works well. Replying on your behalf is where things go wrong, and not subtly: a bot that answers mentions is a bot that can be prompted by anyone who works out it exists. If you want one that posts, look for an approval step, and treat the absence of one as the main fact about that listing rather than a detail.

bots.fitReason: Purpose-built mention monitoring: watches Reddit, X, Hacker News and Bluesky for your product name, competitors and buying-signal phrases, ranked by intent. The name implies replying, so check where the draft/send line sits before you point it at anything public.

Connects X, works out your beat from your recent posts, then sends a weekday end-of-day brief of what you'd want to know. Watching only, which is the safe half of this job — but it monitors your corner of the timeline rather than tracking mentions of a named brand.

Includes an explicit mention watcher and a competitor analyst alongside hook and calendar roles, so monitoring comes bundled with a content crew. It drafts as well as watches; you want that approval step confirmed before it goes near the compose box.

Read-only by design: quiet collectors sample your feed through the day and a 7am brief clusters what mattered. Exactly the low-risk end of this category, though it summarises your feed rather than hunting mentions of you.

Watches your interactions and nearby accounts, then advises who to pay attention to and which replies are worth developing. It is a strategy advisor first, so expect judgement calls rather than a clean alert stream of every mention.

Watches a fixed list of 21 named X accounts twice each weekday and only surfaces high-signal original posts. Account monitoring done properly and it never posts — but the list and the Chinese-language output are fixed to Grok Bot explorers unless you rework it.

Spies a locked list of accounts and queues new followers, which covers the watching side. The caveat is the third automation: it auto-DMs anyone who comments a keyword, so this one writes without an approval step.
